messages.subject: timer() reviewer feedback
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone i used timer function to analysed a songs sample of a bird species. The audio files were recorded at a 48kHz/24bit sample rate in WAV format to achieve high sound quality, we also set an amplitude threshold of 15%.
The reviewer back to me:

 "the authors should manually evaluate the accuracy of the method since the variability of the background noise could affect the measurements"

how can i reply ?

thanks in advance
Sauro Giannerini

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] timer() reviewer feedback
messages.body_plain:
Hello Sauro,
Yes it does make sense. Any automatic treatment should be first controlled with an expert annotation / measurement.
You should then substantial subsample of your dataset, do the measurement manually on this subsamble and compare with timer() output.
HTH
Jerome

messages.subject: Extract Exact timings of calls for sound localisation
messages.subject_clean: Extract Exact timings of calls for sound localisation
messages.body_plain:
Dear Seewave users,

I'm using multiple audio recorders to localise sounds (calls of shorebirds, like in the attached image). I have a recogniser that classifies the presence or absence of the target species at each recorder pretty accurately. To localise, I then need to extract accurate timings that calls arrives on each recorder (from 3sec classifed segments) - wondered if there was a function in Seewave people would recommend to use - it could either pick out peaks of acoustic energy within a frequency band, or inflection points etc., whatever most reliably produced timing of the same point of these calls across different recorders (from the attached image, I'd hope that 12 timings could be extracted).

Also wondered if anyone had ever coded / used a package that did time difference of arrival calculations in R (haven't come across one).

Thanks for any help/advice,
David
